P2199.d: P2199 compares two intake air temperature readings that should be close, typically one in the air mass sensor and one further downstream in the intake manifold or a combined pressure and temperature sensor. Each circuit can be fine on its own; the fault is the disagreement.
s: Scan data shows two clearly different intake temperatures with the engine cold-soaked
c: One temperature sensor drifted or contaminated
Corroded connector or added resistance in one sensor circuit
Calibration issue fixed by a PCM update (e.g. RAM 1500 3.0 EcoDiesel 2020)
Strong heat soak or hot-air leak near one sensor

P219A.d: P219A means the ECM sees mixture differences between the cylinders of bank 1 that are large enough to raise emissions, even if the bank average is fine. CARB phased this monitor in from 25 % of 2011 to all 2014 model-year petrol vehicles (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.1)(C)).
s: Slight rough running or misfire codes when one cylinder is far off
c: One injector clogged, leaking or out of flow tolerance
Compression loss through an intake or exhaust valve
Air leak at one intake runner or gasket
ECM logic or sensor signal issue covered by software or wiring bulletins

P219B.d: P219B is the bank 2 counterpart for V and boxer engines. Ford's 2012 summary shows one way to find it: the ECM watches the fast ripple of the bank's wide-band sensor over windows of roughly 50 revolutions and sets the code when more than 75 % of them fail, after 300 to 700 s of driving at 1000 to 3000 rpm and 20 to 60 % load.
s: Possible misfire codes on bank 2 cylinders
c: Leaking or contaminated injector on bank 2
Interference or damage in the bank 2 A/F sensor wiring
Intake runner or gasket leak at one bank 2 cylinder
PCM calibration addressed by a software update

P219C.d: P219C names cylinder 1 as the one whose mixture departs from the others. Not every system can do that: CARB lets the stored code point only as far as the monitoring method allows, so many engines just log P219A or P219B.
s: Possible P0301 or rough idle if cylinder 1 deviates strongly
c: Cylinder 1 injector clogged, leaking or out of tolerance
Intake runner or injector seal leak at cylinder 1
False detection fixed by ECM reprogramming (e.g. Subaru Crosstrek Hybrid)

P219D.d: P219D singles out cylinder 2. On engines with two banks, whether cylinder 2 sits on bank 1 or bank 2 depends on the maker's numbering, which decides whether P219A or P219B may appear alongside.
s: Reduced power or whistling noise if a charge-air leak is the cause
c: Faulty high-pressure injector at cylinder 2 (direct injection)
Charge-air leak upsetting cylinder filling (e.g. RAM 3.0 Hurricane)
Detection logic corrected by software update (e.g. Hyundai Sonata 2.0T)

P219E.d: P219E points at cylinder 3. Two bulletins show that a mixture code does not always mean a fuel part.
s: Reduced engine power in severe cases
c: Exhaust valve leakage at cylinder 3 (e.g. worn guides on Lexus 8AR-FTS)
Cylinder 3 injector delivering the wrong amount
Incorrect ECM software setting (e.g. Audi 3.0 TFSI)

P219F.d: P219F singles out cylinder 4, the last cylinder on four-cylinder engines. Infiniti issued a bulletin for 2017 to 2018 QX60 with the direct-injection VQ35DD that stored only P219F without any driveability complaint; the remedy was ECM reprogramming followed by the idle air volume learn.
s: Rough running or rattling noise when an injector leaks
No symptom when the cause is software
c: Oversensitive detection fixed by ECM reprogramming (e.g. Infiniti QX60, Hyundai Sonata)
Fouled spark plug as a consequence of a rich cylinder

P21A0.d: P21A0 can only occur on engines with at least five cylinders. VW's 2014 specification books for the Golf, Jetta, Passat and Beetle with the 2.5 litre inline five list P219C to P21A0, one per cylinder, all judged the same way: the ECM briefly leans one cylinder, measures how much rougher the engine runs and derives an individual fuel correction; a result below 0.19 or above 1.50 is a fault.
s: Possible P0305 or slight vibration at idle
c: Ignition or compression weakness at cylinder 5 affecting the roughness test
Software setting corrected by an update (e.g. Audi 3.0 TFSI)

P21A1.d: P21A1 marks cylinder 6, the last cylinder of an inline six or V6. The clearest example comes from the 2025 RAM 1500 with the 3.0 Hurricane twin-turbo inline six: the charge-air cooler housing had a loose crimp that let boost escape, the cylinders filled unevenly and P21A1 set together with other cylinder codes, accompanied by a whistle and lower boost; the cooler was inspected and replaced if needed.
s: Whistling noise and reduced boost with a charge-air leak
c: Charge-air cooler or boost leak (turbo engines, e.g. RAM 3.0 Hurricane)

P21A2.d: P21A2 places a mixture imbalance at cylinder 7, so it only exists on engines with eight or more cylinders. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the bulletin index of the US safety authority NHTSA contains no bulletin that names it.
s: Possible P0307 if the deviation is large
c: Intake runner or injector seal leak at cylinder 7

P21A3.d: P21A3 blames cylinder 8, on a V8 the last cylinder in the numbering. No manufacturer documentation of this code is publicly available, and no bulletin in the NHTSA index refers to it; the basis is the general CARB requirement for detecting cylinder imbalance, phased in for 2011 to 2014 model years with an emission threshold of 3.0 times the FTP standard (4.0 for SULEV II) until 2014 and 1.5 times from 2015.
s: Possible P0308 with a strong deviation
c: Intake leak at the cylinder 8 runner

P21A4.d: P21A4 is reserved for an imbalance at cylinder 9 and can therefore only appear on engines with ten or more cylinders, a small group of V10 and V12 petrol engines. No manufacturer documents the code publicly and no bulletin in the NHTSA index mentions it.
s: Possible P0309 with a large deviation

P21A5.d: P21A5 flags cylinder 10, which on a V10 is the final cylinder and on a V12 sits near the end of its bank. Public manufacturer material for this code does not exist, and the NHTSA bulletin index has no entry for it.
c: Fault in another cylinder of the same bank shifting the result

P21A6.d: P21A6 assigns the imbalance to cylinder 11, which exists only on twelve-cylinder engines. No manufacturer has published how it detects this code, and no NHTSA bulletin names it, so it is a placeholder that J2012 provides for large engines.
s: Possible P0311 with a large deviation

P21A7.d: P21A7 is the last code of the cylinder series that starts with P219C and points to cylinder 12 of a twelve-cylinder engine. There is no public manufacturer description and no NHTSA bulletin for it.

P21A8.d: P21A8 is the general circuit code for the second reductant level sensor, needed only where a DEF tank reports its fill level through more than one sensing element. GM's 6.6L Duramax (LML/LGH) and the 2014 Cruze diesel read three discrete level sensors, numbered 1 to 3 in GM's tables, which corresponds to A to C.
s: DEF system warning message in the cluster
DEF level or range display missing or wrong
c: Damaged or corroded harness or connector at the DEF tank
Level sensor B in the tank assembly failed

P21A9.d: P21A9 flags a level sensor B signal that stays inside its electrical limits but does not fit what else the system knows, such as the states of the other level sensors or the fluid consumed. GM's 2018 Cruze diesel (LH7) stores it in the module running the DEF system, under the name Level Sensor 2 Performance.
s: DEF level shown wrongly or jumping
Fault appears mainly after cold nights
c: Frozen or very cold fluid giving an implausible reading
Level sensor B fouled by crystallised urea or degraded
Control module calibration flagging the sensor too early

P21AA.d: P21AA means the second reductant level sensor reads too low a voltage, which GM takes as a short to ground. GM documents it for the 6.6L Duramax LML and the 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel: the tank level electronics apply a test pulse, and if sensor 2 then shows less than 0.17 V for more than 3 s with over 8 V supply, the ECM receives an error status over CAN.
s: DEF warning message that stays on
DEF range or level display wrong
c: Sensor 2 signal wire chafed through to ground
Fluid or water in the tank connector
Internal short in level sensor B (tank assembly)

P21AB.d: P21AB is the high-side counterpart: GM sets it when level sensor 2 shows an open load (between 3.56 and 4.74 V, read 1.5 ms after the test pulse) or a short to battery voltage (above 4.74 V), each for more than 3 s, as Type A on the 6.6L LML and the 2014 Cruze diesel. GM's preliminary bulletin PIP4887B for 2010–2011 Silverado, Sierra, Express and Savana with the LML or LGH engine names P21AB together with P203D and P
s: Check engine light on at once
Several level sensor codes stored together
c: Open signal wire or spread terminal at the tank connector
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
Level sensor B open inside the tank assembly

P21AC.d: P21AC reports that the level sensor B signal drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents criteria for this code publicly.
s: DEF warning that comes and goes
Check engine light, sometimes only stored code
c: Loose terminal in the tank connector
Harness flexing or rubbing near the tank mounting
Corrosion from fluid creeping into the connector

P21AD.d: P21AD covers the electrical circuit of the third reductant level sensor, so it only exists on tanks with at least three level points. GM's 6.6L Duramax and 2014 Cruze diesel are such cases: the tank electronics test sensors 1 to 3 separately and pass each status to the ECM over CAN.
s: DEF range message missing or implausible
c: Fault in a supply, ground or connector shared by the level sensors
Level sensor C in the tank assembly failed

P21AE.d: P21AE stands for an implausible level sensor C signal whose voltage is still electrically valid. No manufacturer describes a separate check for this code in public material.
s: DEF level display does not match the refill amount
c: Crystallised urea on level sensor C
Partly frozen fluid around the sensor
Level sensor C drifting or degraded

P21AF.d: P21AF is set when level sensor C, called level sensor 3 by GM, reads below 0.17 V right after the tank electronics apply their test pulse, which GM interprets as a short to ground. Supply must be above 8 V and the error must persist for more than 3 s.
s: Check engine light after two trips
c: Sensor 3 signal wire shorted to ground
Water or fluid bridging contacts in the tank connector
Level sensor C shorted inside the tank assembly

P21B0.d: P21B0 means GM's level sensor 3 (sensor C) shows an open circuit or a short to battery: either 3.56 to 4.74 V or more than 4.74 V, measured 1.5 ms after a test pulse, for over 3 s. The 6.6L LML and the 2014 Cruze both rate it Type A, lighting the MIL on the first trip.
s: Check engine light on at once
P203D and P21AB often stored as well
c: Tank connector loose, unplugged or with spread terminals
Sensor 3 signal wire open or shorted to voltage
Level sensor C open inside the tank assembly

P21B1.d: P21B1 marks level sensor C signals that come and go. Public manufacturer criteria do not exist; GM's diesel tables describe sensor 3 only through the steady faults P21AF and P21B0, each filtered over 3 s.
s: DEF warning that appears and clears
c: Harness pinched under a tank strap

P21B2.d: P21B2 is set when the feedback control of a NOx adsorber (lean NOx trap) has not become active within the time the manufacturer allows once its enable conditions are met. CARB requires this check for vehicles with feedback control of the adsorber or its active injection (13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(8.2.3)(A)(i)).
s: Regeneration of the NOx trap delayed or skipped
Higher NOx emissions, possible test failure
c: Fouled or slow oxygen sensor before or after the adsorber
Exhaust not reaching control temperature (short trips, low load)
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensors
Exhaust temperature sensor reporting too low

P21B3.d: P21B3 means the NOx adsorber feedback loop has reached its upper adjustment limit and still misses its target, the case CARB describes in 13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(8.2.3)(A)(iii). In practice the controller asks for more enrichment or longer rich phases than the calibration permits, because the downstream oxygen signal never shows the expected change or the bed stays below its target.
s: Higher fuel consumption from long rich phases
c: NOx adsorber sulphur-loaded or thermally aged
Downstream oxygen sensor responding too slowly
Air leak in the exhaust ahead of the sensors
Too little fuel delivered for the rich phases

P21B4.d: P21B4 reports that the NOx adsorber on bank 1 has run hotter than the manufacturer's protection limit. The risk is greatest during desulphation, when the adsorber is heated on purpose: Eaton patent US7251929 gives about 750 °C as the maximum desulphation temperature, beyond which the adsorber ages thermally, while Cummins aims for roughly 650 °C during regeneration (US7594392).
s: Reduced power while the engine protects the catalyst
Strong smell or heat from the exhaust
c: Too much fuel during regeneration or desulphation
Leaking or dribbling injector on bank 1
Misfire sending unburnt fuel into the exhaust
Exhaust temperature sensor reading too high

P21B5.d: P21B5 is the bank 2 version of the adsorber over-temperature fault and therefore only exists where each cylinder bank feeds its own NOx storage catalyst, which in practice means V engines with two exhaust paths. If only bank 2 overheats, the cause most likely sits on that side: an injector delivering too much, misfire limited to that bank, or a faulty temperature sensor there.
s: Reduced power to protect the catalyst
Uneven exhaust temperatures between the banks
c: Injector on bank 2 delivering too much fuel
Bank 2 exhaust temperature sensor reading too high

P21B6.d: After a cold start, petrol direct-injection and diesel engines deliberately move the moment of injection – for example with an extra late pulse – so that more heat reaches the catalyst. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(11) wants every element of this strategy checked while it runs and reported apart from warm-engine faults.
s: Check engine light after one or more cold starts
Slightly rough idle in the first minute after a cold start
No noticeable fault once the engine is warm
c: Injector of cylinder 1 responds late or inconsistently when cold
Corroded or loose connector or harness at injector 1
Injector driver stage in the engine control module faulty
Engine module software with an overly strict cold-start check

P21B7.d: P21B7 flags cylinder 2 during the cold-start phase only: the injection timing commanded for catalyst heating did not arrive as intended on that cylinder. The heating phase is brief and ends as coolant and catalyst warm up, so the monitor gets one chance per cold start and may need several cold starts before the code is confirmed.
s: Check engine light that appears only after cold starts
Uneven running or slight smoke shortly after starting a cold engine
Code may take several cold starts to return after clearing
c: Injector of cylinder 2 worn or coked, opening late at low temperature
Chafed or high-resistance wiring to injector 2
Weak battery lowering injector supply voltage during and after cranking

P21B8.d: Cylinder 3 is the last cylinder of three-cylinder engines such as Ford's 1.0-litre EcoBoost, a turbo direct-injection unit. There a single cylinder accounts for a third of all combustion events, so a cold-start fault on it tends to be felt more than on larger engines.
s: Noticeable shaking at cold idle, especially on three-cylinder engines
Check engine light after cold starts
c: Injector of cylinder 3 with deposits or a weak coil
Moisture or corrosion in the plug of injector 3
Engine software update available for the cold-start calibration

P21B9.d: Four-cylinder petrol direct injection is the most widespread engine type this code can apply to, and cylinder 4 is its last cylinder. Ford's 2011 OBD summary for its first turbo direct-injection engine explains the background: during catalyst heating the injection timing may be specific to that mode, possibly as two injections with one during the compression stroke, which in turn needs a rail pressure window (checked
s: Check engine light, usually without drivability complaints
Slightly longer catalyst warm-up and possibly higher cold-start emissions
Occasional hesitation right after a cold start
c: Deposits on the tip of injector 4 changing its opening behaviour
Harness fault on the injector 4 circuit
Rail pressure barely inside its window during cold start, affecting the last cylinder first

P21BA.d: P21BA can only occur on engines with at least five cylinders – inline fives, V6, V8 and larger. GM's 4.3-litre V6 and 5.3/6.2-litre V8 direct-injection engines use a dual-pulse injection in open loop after a cold start; a GM bulletin explains that the module watches crankshaft speed in this mode and sets P050D (cold start rough idle) if it varies too much.
s: Check engine light after cold starts
Rough idle during the first seconds after a cold start, possibly together with P050D
c: Injector of cylinder 5 sticking or delivering late when cold
Repair on the wrong injector because of a misread cylinder numbering
Open or high-resistance circuit to injector 5

P21BB.d: Cylinder 6 exists on six-cylinder engines and anything larger – inline sixes and V6 units such as Ford's 3.5-litre EcoBoost petrol or the 3.0-litre EcoDiesel in the Ram 1500. For that diesel FCA listed the warm-engine timing codes P020A–P020F together with the over-advanced and over-retarded codes in a 2021 bulletin whose fix was reprogramming the engine module.
s: Check engine light after cold starts
On diesels, more white smoke or knocking in the first minutes
Hard start or rough idle when cold
c: Outdated engine module software (analogous timing codes were cured by reprogramming)
Injector of cylinder 6 worn, coked or with drifting opening delay
Damaged wiring or connector at injector 6

P21BC.d: From cylinder 7 on, the code is limited to engines with at least seven cylinders – in practice V8, V10, V12 and W12. Common petrol V8 with direct injection are GM's 5.3- and 6.2-litre small blocks, which a GM bulletin describes with dual-pulse injection after a cold start, and Ford's 5.0-litre Coyote, which since 2018 combines port and direct injection.
s: Check engine light after cold starts
Rough cold idle, sometimes with P050D or a cylinder 7 misfire code
c: Direct injector of cylinder 7 slow to open or leaking at low temperature
Chafed or heat-damaged wiring to injector 7
Fault in the high-voltage injector driver of the engine module

P21BD.d: P21BD covers cylinder 8, the last cylinder of a V8. GM's 2025 diesel tables show how close an existing monitor comes to this code: during cold start the module compares requested and scheduled start of injection, with every cylinder from A to H included in the enable checks, and a deviation beyond ±4 in 88 of 176 samples sets the lamp in the first trip.
s: Check engine light after cold starts
Rough running or smoke in the first minute after a cold start
c: Injector of cylinder 8 with slow or varying response
Connector or wiring fault at injector 8
Cold-start calibration in the engine module needing an update

P21BE.d: A ninth cylinder exists only on V10, V12 and W12 engines, so P21BE is limited to a handful of models. Petrol engines in this class with direct injection include the 5.2-litre V10 of Lamborghini and Audi (Huracán, R8, S6 and S8) and the 6.3-litre W12 FSI of the Audi A8, which feeds its injectors from two high-pressure pumps and two rails.
s: Check engine light after cold starts
Slightly uneven idle while the engine is cold
c: Direct injector of cylinder 9 with deposits or slow response
Low pressure on the rail feeding cylinder 9 (engines with two rails)
Wiring or connector fault at injector 9

P21BF.d: Cylinder 10 is the last cylinder of a V10 and exists otherwise only on twelve-cylinder engines. V10 engines are rare: Ford's 6.8-litre truck V10 (firing order 1-6-5-10-2-7-3-8-4-9, in the E-Series until 2019) and the 5.2-litre direct-injection V10 of Lamborghini and Audi.
s: Check engine light after one or more cold starts
Uneven idle until the engine warms up
c: Injector of cylinder 10 aged or contaminated
Wiring or connector problem at injector 10
Engine module software needing a cold-start calibration update

P21C0.d: P21C0 applies only to twelve-cylinder engines (V12 or W12), since passenger-car engines with exactly eleven cylinders do not exist. Examples with direct injection are BMW's N74 twin-turbo V12, found in the BMW 760i and in Rolls-Royce models such as Ghost, Wraith and Dawn, and the 6.3-litre W12 FSI.
s: Check engine light after cold starts
Barely noticeable on the road; a twelve-cylinder engine masks a single cylinder well
c: Direct injector of cylinder 11 with changed opening behaviour
Heat-damaged wiring or connector at injector 11
Injector driver for cylinder 11 in the engine control module faulty

P21C1.d: Cylinder 12 is the last cylinder of V12 and W12 engines. Direct-injection V12 include Ferrari's F140 family (FF, F12berlinetta, 812 Superfast) and BMW's N74; among W engines there is the 6.3-litre W12 FSI.
s: Check engine light after cold starts
Hardly any drivability change, at most a slightly uneven cold idle
c: Injector of cylinder 12 with deposits or worn needle
Damaged wiring at the end of the cylinder bank (injector 12)
Cold-start calibration of the engine module out of date

P21C2.d: P21C2 concerns the control line of the relay that supplies current to the DEF heaters. The control module drives the relay coil through an output stage and checks whether the circuit reacts; an open circuit means the coil, its wiring or a connector has lost continuity, so the heaters cannot be energised.
s: DEF system warning, especially at low ambient temperature
Frozen DEF thaws slowly, dosing begins late after a cold start
c: Relay coil burnt open or relay not seated in its socket
Broken control wire between module and relay
Corroded or loose terminals at relay box or module connector
Faulty output stage in the controlling module

P21C3.d: P21C3 is the low-side fault on the control line of the DEF heater relay: the signal is pulled toward ground, for example by a chafed wire touching the frame or a shorted relay coil, so the relay no longer follows the command. Ford's 2023 diesel summary uses the same continuous check as for P21C2, but here the relay stage is on, every heater has been told to stay off, and still more than 6 A of heater current is measu
s: DEF heating inactive or running when not commanded
Blown fuse in the heater supply
c: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Relay coil with internal short or welded contacts
Water or salt in the relay or heater connector
Output stage of the controlling module faulty

P21C4.d: P21C4 means the control side of the DEF heater relay shows voltage when it should be dead. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets it when the relay stage and all heaters are off and the heater circuit still carries more than 5 V, within at most 5 s; a short to the battery feed or contacts that no longer open are the classic reasons.
s: Code appears shortly after a DEF control unit was replaced
Additional communication code such as U11C1 stored
c: Replacement dosing control unit not programmed or with outdated software (FCA)
Control or heater wire shorted to battery voltage
Internal fault in the controlling module

P21C5.d: P21C5 is a plausibility code: the level sensor A reports valid readings, yet they hardly move when the fluid in the tank should be sloshing. GM spells this out for the ultrasonic sensor in its 2025 diesel tables, where it is sensor 1.
s: Check engine light on after two drives
DEF gauge stays at the same value while fluid is being used
DEF warning messages in the instrument cluster
c: Level sensor calibration in the engine software (update available, e.g. Jaguar)
Ultrasonic level sensor in the tank unit faulty
Crystal deposits or gas bubbles disturbing the echo
Fluid partly frozen or slush around the sensor

P21C6.d: P21C6 applies only to DEF tanks with a second level measurement, labelled B. It is stored when that second reading is electrically fine but stays frozen at one value although the module expects it to change.
s: DEF gauge implausible or not moving
DEF warning in the instrument cluster
c: Second level sensing element in the tank unit faulty
Float or contact held by crystals or debris
Calibration of the level evaluation needs a software update

P21C7.d: P21C7 flags a break in the control line of the power relay, or group of relays, that supplies the DEF control module and the loads behind it. Ford's 2023 diesel summary evaluates it inside the same continuous heater relay check as P21C2 to P21C4, so on that design the relay also feeds the heating circuits.
s: DEF heating and dosing do not work
SCR warning and countdown to restricted starting or speed
c: Relay defective or missing from its socket
Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay
Blown fuse in the relay or module feed
Driver in the controlling module faulty

P21C8.d: P21C8 means the control line of the DEF module's power relay, or relays, sits too close to ground. No manufacturer documents P21C8 publicly.
s: DEF system without power or permanently powered
Flat battery after the vehicle has been parked
c: Control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Moisture in relay socket or module connector
Output stage in the controlling module faulty

P21C9.d: P21C9 is stored when the control line of the DEF module's power relay, or relays, carries more voltage than the driver state allows, typically because the wire touches a battery feed or the driver can no longer pull it down. No manufacturer documents P21C9 publicly.
s: DEF pump or module audible or active with the engine off
c: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage circuit
Relay contacts welded, switched side stays live
Driver in the controlling module shorted

P21CA.d: P21CA is the general code for the supply feed of the DEF control module: the voltage arriving at the module is missing or unusable, without the module assigning it to the low or high case. Volvo and Mack trucks use it, as P21CA00, on the aftertreatment control module that runs the SCR system.
s: Several sensor communication codes at the same time
c: Loose or corroded battery or ground connections of the module
Weak batteries or insufficient charging voltage
Faulty in-line fuse or damaged supply wire

P21CB.d: P21CB says the DEF control module receives too little supply voltage. GM measures it as a difference to system voltage: in the 2018 diesel tables a gap above 3 V between battery voltage and the supply of the SCR power module, seen in 40 of 50 samples taken every 100 ms with the powertrain relay in range and cranking excluded, sets the code; the 2025 tables apply the same 3 V gap to the permanent DEF supply against th
s: DEF dosing or heating drops out intermittently
Further undervoltage or communication codes from the SCR system
c: Voltage drop at fuse, terminal or ground of the module feed
Weak battery or low charging voltage
Damaged or corroded supply wire to the module
Internal voltage measurement of the module faulty

P21CC.d: P21CC is the overvoltage counterpart of P21CB: the DEF control module sees a supply above what its electronics are designed for. Ford's 2023 diesel summary checks the reductant pump controller in a continuous loop and sets P21CC once its supply exceeds 19 V, deciding within 5 s.
s: Battery or charging warning, bulbs unusually bright
c: Jump start or charging with excessive voltage
Loose battery terminal causing voltage spikes

P21CD.d: The DEF quality module measures the urea concentration in the tank and, on many tanks, shares a housing with the level sensor. P21CD reports that its supply voltage is too low.
s: DEF quality or level warning in the instrument cluster
Communication code for the quality module stored as well
c: Water and corrosion in the quality module connector (Ford C4851)
Damaged tank harness or supply wire

P21CE.d: P21CE says the DEF quality module as a unit is not working properly: it is supplied and talking to the controller, but its self-test or the plausibility of its output fails, so the controller cannot rely on the concentration it reports. This differs from P206B to P206D, which grade the measured concentration, and from P21CD, which concerns the module supply.
s: DEF system error message in the display
c: Contaminated or degraded DEF disturbing the measurement
Crystals or air bubbles on the sensing element
Poor contact at the module connector

P21CF.d: P21CF flags an open drive circuit of the second injector on cylinder 1. Which of the two injectors is B depends on the maker: Ford gives the letter to the port injector and keeps A, coded P0201, for direct injection, whereas Mitsubishi calls its direct injectors B and files open circuits under the low code P21DB.
s: Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 1, often with P0301
Further harness codes stored at the same time
c: Chafed or broken wire in the port injector harness (on the Bronco Sport near the transmission cover)
Open coil in the cylinder 1 port injector
Loose or corroded plug at the injector
Faulty driver stage in the engine module or separate injector module

P21D0.d: P21D0 is the open-circuit code for the B injector of cylinder 2. Where that cylinder sits varies: GM's small-block V8 alternates odd and even numbers between the banks, so cylinder 2 opens the right bank, while Ford's V6 and V8 count one bank first and place it next to cylinder 1.
s: Misfire on cylinder 2, mainly at idle and light load
c: Port injector of cylinder 2 with an open winding
Broken wire or pushed-back terminal in the injector harness
Output stage in the engine or injection module failed

P21D1.d: P21D1 concerns the B injector of cylinder 3, which on Ford's 1.5 EcoBoost three-cylinder is the last one in the block. That engine combines port and direct fuel, and Ford names the port injectors B.
s: Rough running or misfire on cylinder 3
With harness damage also transmission codes or no crank
c: Harness damage affecting several injectors at once (Ford Bronco Sport, transmission cover)
Open coil in the cylinder 3 port injector

P21D2.d: P21D2 reports an open in the drive circuit of the B injector on cylinder 4. On four-cylinder engines with dual injection it is the last of the set, for example Ford's 2.0 EcoBoost from 2022 or the 2.3 introduced for the 2024 Mustang, both of which added port injectors to direct injection.
c: Open winding in the cylinder 4 port injector
Wire broken at a bend or clip near the intake manifold

P21D3.d: P21D3 can only appear on engines with at least five cylinders and two injectors per cylinder. Documented users are Ford's dual-injection V6 and V8 engines (2.7 and 3.5 EcoBoost of the second generation, 5.0 V8 from 2018) and GM's supercharged LT5 V8.
s: Fuel trim of one bank shifted
c: Open coil in the cylinder 5 port injector
Broken wire in the bank harness of the port injectors
Output stage in the engine or injection module failed

P21D4.d: P21D4 is the last B injector code on a six-cylinder engine. Ford's second-generation 2.7 and 3.5 EcoBoost V6 combine port and direct injection, label the port injectors B and test this circuit together with P21CF to P21D3, continuously above 11 V within 5 s; on these engines cylinder 6 is the rear cylinder of the second bank.
c: Port injector of cylinder 6 open internally
Damaged wire at the rear of the engine, hard to inspect
Connector not fully latched after earlier work on the intake

P21D5.d: P21D5 belongs to V8 engines with a second injector per cylinder. Two are documented: Ford's 5.0 V8, which gained direct injection alongside its port injectors in 2018, and GM's 2019 LT5, the supercharged Corvette ZR1 engine with primary direct and supplemental port injection.
s: Misfire on cylinder 7, on the LT5 mostly under high load
c: Open winding in the cylinder 7 port injector
Broken wire or terminal in the port injector harness of that bank
Separate fuel injection control module faulty (GM LT5)

P21D6.d: P21D6 is the highest B injector code that any manufacturer documents publicly: both Ford's port injector check (P21CF to P21D6) and GM's LT5 injection module list end here. On the LT5 the port injectors exist to add fuel under boost beyond what the direct system and its mechanical pump can deliver, so an open cylinder 8 injector shows up mainly at high load, where that cylinder can run lean and lose power; GM stores
s: Misfire or lean running on cylinder 8 under load
c: Wire damage at the rear of the engine near the firewall
Output of the engine or separate injection module failed

P21D7.d: P21D7 would mark an open drive circuit of the second injector on cylinder 9, which presupposes at least nine cylinders. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the published Ford and GM lists stop at cylinder 8 (P21D6).
c: Open coil in the second injector of cylinder 9
Broken wire or terminal in the injector harness
Driver stage in the engine control module failed

P21D8.d: P21D8 covers the second injector of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
c: Second injector of cylinder 10 open internally
Wiring or connector fault at the cylinder 10 injector
Output stage in the engine control module failed

P21D9.d: P21D9 is reserved for an open circuit of the second injector on cylinder 11 and therefore only makes sense on twelve-cylinder engines with dual injection. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no available source names a twelve-cylinder engine that uses it.
c: Open coil in the second injector of cylinder 11
Damaged injector harness or loose plug
Faulty driver in the engine control module

P21DA.d: P21DA closes the circuit/open series of the second injectors with cylinder 12. It requires a twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder; no manufacturer documents this code publicly and no available source names such an engine using it.
c: Second injector of cylinder 12 with open coil
Wire or terminal fault in the injector harness
Output stage of the controlling module failed

P21DB.d: P21DB means the drive circuit of the B injector on cylinder 1 is pulled toward ground. Two makers document it, with opposite meanings of B.
s: Reduced torque when several cylinders are affected (Mitsubishi)
c: Injector wire chafed through to ground
Injector winding open or shorted to its housing
Engine or injection control module faulty

P21DC.d: P21DC is the high-side fault of the cylinder 1 B injector: the line carries voltage where the control unit expects it to be low, typically from a short to supply or between the two injector wires. On GM's 2019 LT5 V8 the FICM injection module looks at the low side of the supplemental injector while its driver is off; less than 0.5 Ohm toward power in 20 of 25 samples sets a Type A fault, so that injector can no longe
s: Torque limited if more cylinders fail (Mitsubishi)
c: Injector control wire shorted to a supply wire
Both injector wires shorted together in the harness
Driver stage of the control module damaged

P21DD.d: P21DD means heater A of the DEF system, which Ford and GM both assign to the tank heater (circuit 1), draws less current than expected while switched on, so it is likely open or barely heating. GM's 2025 diesel tables set it when heater 1 current stays below 0.75 A for 40 samples of 0.1 s during a positive command, Type A with MIL after one trip; the 2014 tables flagged an open tank heater when its conductance fell t
s: DEF stays frozen longer in winter, dosing starts late
DEF warning messages after cold starts
c: Water and corrosion in the pump and heater connector (Ford C3613)
Missing heater supply due to relay, fuse or wiring fault
Heater driver in the control module faulty

P21DE.d: P21DE is the low fault of the cylinder 2 B injector circuit. In Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross manual, B means the direct injector; the code covers both a break and a grounded wire on the two DI lines of cylinder 2, held for 2 s at 10 to 16.5 V, while the port injector of the same cylinder reports P0264.
s: Possible fuel smell or rich running if an injector stays open
c: Injector line of cylinder 2 touching ground
Fault at the intermediate connector of the injector harness

P21DF.d: P21DF is set when the cylinder 2 B injector circuit shows a short toward supply. Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross applies it to the direct high-pressure injector and stores it after a 2 s short with the ignition on and the driver supply above 10 V; troubleshooting first inspects the negative DI wire of cylinder 2 up to the engine module and names the injector, the harness and the ECM as possible causes.
s: Less pulling power with multiple faults
c: Negative injector line of cylinder 2 shorted to supply
ECM or injection module driver defective

P21E0.d: P21E0 reports a low circuit state on the B injector of cylinder 3. Mitsubishi lists it for the 2022 Eclipse Cross as the direct injector code and does not use the open code P21D1, so an interrupted wire and a short to ground both end up here once they last 2 s.
c: Cylinder 3 injector wire broken or shorted to ground
Injector of cylinder 3 with open or shorted coil

P21E1.d: P21E1 is the high fault on the cylinder 3 B injector circuit. In Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross that is the direct high-pressure injector, and the module reacts to a short circuit lasting 2 s, checked with 10 to 16.5 V battery voltage.
s: Torque reduction if several injectors fail (Mitsubishi)
c: Cylinder 3 injector line shorted to supply voltage
Damaged driver in the control module

P21E2.d: P21E2 is the low fault of the B injector on cylinder 4, the last cylinder of an inline four. It is the final direct injector low code in Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross list, which uses B for the high-pressure injectors and sets it for an open or a short to ground lasting 2 s.
s: Noticeably less power with several codes (port injection only)
c: Cylinder 4 injector wire open or shorted to ground
Intermediate connector fault affecting several cylinders

P21E3.d: P21E3 marks a high circuit state on the cylinder 4 B injector, normally a short to a supply line. On Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross, where B is the direct high-pressure injector, the fault must persist 2 s; it closes the manual's list of direct injector circuit codes for the four cylinders.
s: Engine runs with reduced torque if further cylinders are affected
c: Cylinder 4 injector line shorted to a supply wire
Driver stage in the ECM or injection module damaged

P21E4.d: P21E4 flags a low state on the circuit of the second (B) injector serving cylinder 5. The only public OBD summary that lists it is GM's for the 2019 Corvette ZR1, whose supercharged LT5 V8 pairs direct injectors with port injectors and drives the supplemental ones from a separate fuel injection control module (FICM).
s: Rich running or fuel trim pulled back on bank 1
Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 5
c: Low-side wire of the cylinder 5 B injector touching ground
Injector winding shorted to its housing
Moisture or corrosion in the injector connector
Driver stage in the injection control module faulty

P21E5.d: P21E5 means the cylinder 5 B injector circuit is pulled toward supply voltage. GM documents it for the LT5 V8 of the 2019 Corvette ZR1: the FICM looks at the low side of that injector while its driver is off and treats 0.5 Ohm or less toward power as a short.
s: Cylinder 5 lean or hesitant at full load
c: Low-side wire of the cylinder 5 B injector shorted to a supply wire
Supply and control wire of the injector bridged in the harness
Injector coil shorted across its terminals
Damaged output stage in the injection control module

P21E6.d: P21E6 reports that the B injector circuit of cylinder 6 has found a path to ground. In GM's 2019 tables for the Corvette ZR1 LT5, cylinder 6 is the third position on the right bank, which GM counts as bank 2.
s: Rich condition on bank 2, possibly fuel smell
Fouled spark plug or misfire on cylinder 6
c: Cylinder 6 B injector harness chafed against engine metal
Internal short to ground inside the injector
Injection control module output stuck low

P21E7.d: P21E7 is stored when the B injector of cylinder 6 shows a short toward power. GM's 2019 Corvette ZR1 with the LT5 V8 is the documented user; there the FICM checks the low side only in the driver-off state, flags 0.5 Ohm or less to power, and needs at least 11 V at the powertrain relay with the engine running.
s: Lean condition on bank 2 under load
c: Cylinder 6 B injector control wire in contact with a live wire
Shorted turns in the injector coil
Output stage of the injection control module damaged by the short

P21E8.d: P21E8 covers a low, ground-side fault on the cylinder 7 B injector. GM lists it for the 2019 Corvette ZR1, where the LT5 V8 carries a direct and a supplemental injector per cylinder and cylinder 7 is the rearmost cylinder of the left bank (bank 1).
c: Cylinder 7 B injector wire grounded at the rear of the engine

P21E9.d: P21E9 indicates that the low side of the cylinder 7 B injector carries supply voltage. On GM's 2019 Corvette ZR1 LT5, the FICM declares this when it sees 0.5 Ohm or less to power with the driver off, provided the engine runs and the powertrain relay delivers 11 V or more; Type A, one trip.
c: Cylinder 7 B injector control wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector coil with too low resistance

P21EA.d: P21EA is the ground-short code for the B injector of cylinder 8 and the last low code in GM's 2019 FICM table for the Corvette ZR1 LT5, because the V8 ends there. Cylinder 8 is the rearmost of the right bank (bank 2).
s: Hard hot start or misfire on cylinder 8
c: Cylinder 8 B injector wiring chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion in the cylinder 8 injector plug

P21EB.d: P21EB is set when the cylinder 8 B injector circuit is shorted toward power. It closes GM's run of B-injector codes for the 2019 Corvette ZR1 LT5: the FICM sees the switched-off low side within 0.5 Ohm of supply in 20 of 25 samples and stores a Type A fault, lighting the MIL in the first trip.
c: Cylinder 8 B injector control wire shorted to a feed wire
Shared harness connector shorted when several injectors are affected

P21EC.d: P21EC signals a low circuit state, usually a grounded wire or, depending on the maker, also a break, on the B injector of cylinder 9. It can only occur on an engine with at least nine cylinders and two injectors per cylinder.
s: Misfire or rough running on cylinder 9
Mixture deviation on the bank of cylinder 9
c: Cylinder 9 B injector wire shorted to ground
Broken wire, if the maker reports opens under the low code
Injector coil shorted to housing or open

P21ED.d: P21ED is defined for a B injector circuit on cylinder 9 that reads high, meaning the control side is shorted to supply or, on some designs, the two injector wires touch. No manufacturer publishes thresholds or vehicles for it.
s: Cylinder 9 lean in mixed injection operation
c: Control wire of the cylinder 9 B injector shorted to power
Both injector wires bridged in the harness
Driver stage in the control unit faulty

P21EE.d: P21EE is the low-circuit code for the B injector of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. In practice that points to a ten-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder, of which only Lamborghini's Huracán is documented: its V10 pairs a direct injector with a port injector at each cylinder and was presented as the first V10 to combine both.
s: Rough running or misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)
Fuel trim deviation on the second bank
c: Damaged or corroded injector connector on cylinder 10

P21EF.d: P21EF stands for a high reading on the B injector circuit of cylinder 10. No public manufacturer document covers it, so the exact threshold is unknown; the closest documented model is GM's LT5 V8, where a switched-off low side within 0.5 Ohm of supply counts as a short and sets a Type A fault.
s: Cylinder 10 weak or misfiring under load
Lean mixture on the second bank
c: Cylinder 10 B injector control wire touching a live circuit
Short inside a connector shared by several injectors
Output stage overloaded by the short

P21F0.d: P21F0 is reserved for a low state, typically a wire touching ground, in the B injector circuit of cylinder 11. Setting it requires at least eleven cylinders with two injectors each, so in practice a V12 or W12 with combined port and direct injection.
c: Cylinder 11 B injector wire shorted to ground
Injector with internal short to ground
Code read on an engine without a cylinder 11 B injector (scan tool or maker-specific use)

P21F1.d: P21F1 describes a cylinder 11 B injector circuit that sits too high, i.e. its switched side is shorted to supply.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 11 B injector shorted to power

P21F2.d: P21F2 is the generic code for a low circuit state, usually a grounded control wire, at the B injector of cylinder 12. It would need a twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder, and none could be documented: the V12s from Lamborghini and Aston Martin inject into the ports only.
s: Hybrid warning instead, if the code is a McLaren battery fault
c: Cylinder 12 B injector wire shorted to ground
Manufacturer-specific use of the number (McLaren Artura high-voltage battery)

P21F3.d: P21F3 ends the B injector series of SAE J2012: a high signal on the cylinder 12 circuit, caused by a short to supply on the switched side. The series runs from P21CF to P21DA for opens and from P21DB to P21F3 for low/high pairs; the A injector equivalent here is P0295.
c: Control wire of the cylinder 12 B injector shorted to supply
Driver stage damaged by a lasting short

P21F4.d: P21F4 reports that the second fuel path on bank 1 needs more added fuel than its adaptation may supply once the engine has left idle, in the part-load range. Engines with port and direct injection learn a correction for each path; Ford calls its direct system A and its port system B.
s: Weak performance or hesitation at part load
Often stored together with P2177 or P0087
c: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Port injectors of bank 1 restricted or delivering too little
Pressure in the low-pressure (port) fuel rail too low
Air mass sensor reading too low

P21F5.d: P21F5 is the rich limit for the second fuel path of bank 1 in the part-load zone above idle: the learned correction already removes as much fuel as allowed, yet the front sensor still sees surplus fuel. Audi lists the code for the 2.5 TFSI in the 2017 to 2018 RS 3 and TT RS, whose manifold injectors run on a 7 bar rail beside the high-pressure system, and cures it by reprogramming the engine control module (bulletin
c: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Port injector on bank 1 leaking or sticking open
Pressure in the low-pressure rail above specification
Air mass sensor reading too high

P21F6.d: P21F6 is the bank 2 form of P21F4 and only exists on V or flat engines whose cylinder banks each have their own front oxygen sensor and two injection paths. Here the part-load correction of the second path on bank 2 has reached its lean limit.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the bank 2 injector harness
Low pressure in the shared port fuel rail (if bank 1 also lean)

P21F7.d: P21F7 sets when the second fuel path on bank 2 has to remove more fuel above idle than its rich limit permits. It needs an engine with two banks, separate front sensors and dual injection; inline engines such as Audi's 2.5 TFSI only have the bank 1 codes.
c: Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
Low-pressure regulation too high (if bank 1 also rich)

P21F8.d: P21F8 covers the idle zone: the second fuel path of bank 1 needs more extra fuel at idle than its adaptation allows. Airflow at idle is so small that a fixed amount of unmetered air or a slightly sluggish injector shifts the mixture a lot, which is why makers learn idle separately from part load.
c: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Unmetered air entering behind the air mass sensor
Port injector on bank 1 delivering too little
Low pressure in the port fuel rail

P21F9.d: P21F9 reports that bank 1's second fuel path runs rich at idle even though its correction has already reached the lower limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi's 2.5 TFSI bulletin lists only the lean idle code P21F8 and the off-idle pair.
c: Port injector on bank 1 dripping after closing
Low-pressure fuel regulation holding too much pressure
Fuel vapour entering via crankcase ventilation (fuel-diluted oil)

P21FA.d: P21FA is the bank 2 version of the idle lean check for the second fuel path. It applies to engines with two cylinder banks, a front oxygen sensor per bank and dual injection, such as Ford's 5.0 V8, which has combined port and direct injection since 2018.
c: Intake leak at bank 2 runners or gasket
Partly blocked port injector on bank 2
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading lean

P21FB.d: P21FB means bank 2's second fuel path is rich at idle while its correction already sits at the rich limit. The code requires an engine with a separate front sensor per bank and two injection paths; no maker documents it publicly.
c: Port injector on bank 2 leaking or sticking open
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
Low-pressure regulation too high or fuel from crankcase ventilation (if both banks rich)

P21FC.d: P21FC is the lean check of bank 1's second fuel path in the upper load zone, the third cell next to idle (P21F8) and part load (P21F4). Under high load, delivery capacity matters most: a weak lift pump, a clogged filter or a low-pressure rail that sags at high flow show up here first.
s: Hesitation or power loss at full load
c: Weak in-tank lift pump or clogged fuel filter
Port rail pressure dropping at high flow
Port injectors on bank 1 flowing too little
Charge air leak behind the air mass sensor

P21FD.d: P21FD sets when the second fuel path on bank 1 is still rich at higher load although its learned correction has already taken away the permitted maximum. No manufacturer documents the code publicly.
c: Air mass sensor reading too high at large airflow
Low-pressure regulator holding too much pressure

P21FE.d: P21FE is the bank 2 counterpart of P21FC: in the upper load zone the second injection path on bank 2 needs more enrichment than its adaptation may supply. It can only appear on two-bank engines with per-bank sensors and dual injection.
s: Loss of pull at full throttle
c: Harness or connector fault on bank 2 injectors
Weak shared supply (lift pump, filter, low-pressure sensor) if both banks lean

P21FF.d: P21FF closes the series: bank 2's second fuel path is rich in the upper load range although its correction already removes the largest reduction allowed. No manufacturer publishes criteria for it.
c: Port injectors on bank 2 over-delivering at long pulse widths
Excessive pressure in the shared low-pressure rail
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
